findings.summary: In the article's code block the <code> element inside <pre class="code-block"> keeps the browser's default 'monospace' family (Courier-like serif mono), because the mono family is set on the <pre> but the UA rule on <code> overrides inheritance. styles.json records a bare 'monospace' family at 2.68% of text, which no earlier margin-notes run has. The font gate passes only because 'monospace' counts as a fallback. The reference's code panels use the template mono throughout.

On the record-detail screen the tab list sits about 8 to 10px under the meta line ('Internal Platform · Owned by …'), so the header has no bottom padding before the tabs and they read as attached to the meta. The spec asks for a space.40 bottom on the page header. The 1.0.0 sample of the same screen left a clear gap there. This is agent variance in an area the update did not touch, on one screen of one app.

On the dashboard overview the header's 'Refresh' button sits on the lower edge of the bloom, light and dark. In the reference the bloom sits beside or behind content cards and never under a control. Everywhere else the bloom stays in the empty right margin of the header band.

notes: Update goal reached. The package now places studio details by screen moment, and the agents placed them correctly in every app without per-app instructions. Home, index and collection screens (the blog home, the store catalog, the dashboard overview, projects and team) get the bloom in the header band plus a Caveat note on the lead that restates it ('build, write, work well', 'made for daily use', 'health, all teams', 'every initiative', 'the whole team'). The serif word with its swash appears only in multi-word home h1s ('Field Notes', 'Shop all goods'). The featured item is taped and lifted (blog). The editorial title gets a serif word plus one serif pull-quote (articles). Settings screens get no bloom, serif or tape, and one note--below on the section navigation ('pick a section') that stays inside the narrow column. Record-detail and checkout screens (product, project, cart with items) get nothing. The page-level empty state (empty cart) keeps its bloom, 1 tape strip and a note on its button, as the Empty state spec says.

No regression against the last comparable runs. The published 1.1.0 has runs only for the docs and landing apps, so these four apps were compared with the 1.0.0 runs (showcase/runs/margin-notes/1.0.0/*/20261012-134307). The dashboard overview, stat cards, chart, projects table, mobile stacked rows, settings forms, billing, dialogs, toasts and error states match or beat 1.0.0. Fixed since the 1.0.0 critic notes: the 'This device' badge now has its gap (settings-security), and the dark row hover is visible (state-row-hover-desktop-dark). The one screen where the 1.0.0 sample looked better is filed above as a minor (tab spacing on record detail).

Reference fidelity: recognizable and not a copy. It has the warm paper, the tight grotesk with ink actions, hairline cards, mono eyebrows and machine values, ink chips, tray segmented controls, Caveat notes with hooked arrows, tape, and a grained watercolor bloom with a darker rim (blog home-d1, commerce cart-d1). The bloom is still smaller than the reference p1 bloom, which is acceptable for app headers and unchanged from earlier versions. The dark bloom reads as a smoky slate wash, also unchanged.

The dashboard shows no serif word, because all its h1s are single words and rule 6 needs 2 or more. This is the spec working as designed (the rule answers an earlier critic finding) and is unchanged from 1.0.0. It is not a finding.

Unchanged agent misses already listed in the 1.0.0 critic notes, not re-raised: some rule-7 mono and sans slips (product spec row '40 × 35 × 15 cm' in sans, team 'Active projects' counts in sans, billing 'Amount' header in mono); the mobile success badge squeezed into the fixed action bar with text faintly showing through the bar (settings state-profile-saved-mobile-light); the dialog scrim stopping at y=900 and fixed elements drawn mid-page in full-page captures (capture artifacts).
Measured layout defects: none were reported, and none were seen on the screenshots.
Motion: no animations in any app (shots.json motion.animations 0) and no frame sequences to judge. The spec asks for static studio marks, so this is correct.

Evidence gaps for the lead: (1) eval-1.md and eval-1.json for 1.2.0-rc.1 have no functional-preservation (smoke test) row in any app, while the 1.1.0 eval does. The brief says 'all passed', but the base-app smoke contract was not recorded for this candidate. Confirm it before calling the gates passed. (2) pipeline/pigment-study/reference/illustrations/ is empty, so drawing crops were compared with the reference screenshots (p1, p2, p3) instead of reference crops.
Verdict basis: no blocker and no major. The three findings are minors from one sample, none caused by the spec.
